נטילת צפרנים בחול המועד. ובו ב סעיפים:

(1) SA — permitted, etc. There on s.v. the halachah follows R' Yosi on the festival; and though they said there in Genuztra it is forbidden — Rif wrote it refers to a mourner; therefore we say there "I was standing," etc. — meaning there was no knife there; therefore no difficulty that four are forbidden in doubt; and this is what he wrote "even," etc.; proof from what is written below "they requested a knife" — and where there is a knife permitted for all, likewise for his nails; see Nimukey Yosef:

(ב) Between A and B. Name:

(3) But, etc. — they also explain on chol hamoed; see Tosafot there s.v. uv'ginustri, etc.:

(4) Whether with a knife, etc. — see Rashi s.v. ginustri, etc., and Tosafot s.v. uv'ginustra explained in Arukh, etc.; and likewise for a knife now that the way is to cut with a knife; Hagahat Semak wrote so, and such is primary that we require a change as written; and in Genuztra forbidden means with scissors; R' Baruch explained likewise with a knife since so is the way to cut with a knife:

(5) If not so, etc. — in the name of Tosafot there it is no worse than transferring hair of the armpit and the private area which are permitted; see those Tosafot; and I heard in the name of Rashba, etc., that Yerushalmi teaches, etc. — meaning armpit hair and private area; Maharam disagrees and explained specifically that Israel may not cut for her with knife or scissors, but she herself may not; and so Yoreh De'ah siman 393 seif 6; but here one may rely on the permissive views since there are permissive views everywhere; see Darkei Moshe:
